title: Scenario-Based Questions
definition: Interview questions that present a complex, real-world business problem and ask you to design the API architecture to solve it.
simpleExplanation: There is no single 'right' answer. The interviewer wants to hear your thought process. They want to see if you can balance performance, security, and scalability.
realWorldExample: Scenario: 'We are building a live sports scoreboard for the Super Bowl. Millions of users will have the app open simultaneously. How do you deliver the live score?'

basic: Scenario: You need to upload a 5 Gigabyte video file to an API. How do you handle it?
intermediate: Scenario: Your frontend needs to know when a background video rendering task finishes. Do you use Polling or WebSockets?

answers.question: Upload 5GB file?
answers.answer: You do NOT send it through your Node.js API server, as that will block the server and run out of memory. You should request a 'Pre-signed URL' from the backend, and have the frontend upload the massive file directly to AWS S3, bypassing your backend entirely.

answers.question: Polling or WebSockets?
answers.answer: Neither. Video rendering takes minutes or hours. Keeping a WebSocket open that long is inefficient and fragile on mobile networks. Short Polling destroys the server. The best approach is Long Polling, or Server-Sent Events (SSE), or simply using Push Notifications if it's a mobile app.

codeExample:
/*
  Scenario:
  "Design the REST API routes for a library system where users can check out books."
  
  Answer:
  - GET    /books                (List all books)
  - GET    /books/:id            (Get specific book details)
  - POST   /users/:id/checkouts  (Action: A user checks out a book. Body: { bookId })
  - GET    /users/:id/checkouts  (List all books a specific user has checked out)
  - DELETE /users/:id/checkouts/:bookId (Action: User returns the book)
*/
